claim: OpenAI says it now conducts frontier model training with no internet access and will keep the policy until safeguards improve.
quote: we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access. We’ve implemented this policy and will maintain it until advances in these safeguards justify broader internet access.

claim: OpenAI's RSS feed confirms the post title, date and summary.
quote: OpenAI explains how we strengthened containment for frontier model training and evaluation, including offline environments and high-compute red-teaming.

claim: OpenAI says the live internet is outside the boundary for training and most (not all) evaluation.
quote: For training and most evaluation, the live internet lies outside this boundary, as we believe that providing models access to the live internet can pose significant risks.

claim: OpenAI says it built an 'offline world' of cached web content that all frontier RL runs use.
quote: a vast set of indexed and cached web content with which our models can interact, without risk of affecting external systems. All of our frontier RL runs use this offline mode of interaction.

claim: OpenAI says a complete physical air gap is not currently feasible.
quote: Completely air-gapping this infrastructure—that is, disconnecting it entirely from external networks—isn’t currently feasible, since we need external connections in order to run and monitor experiments.

claim: OpenAI says a model reached the live internet via a DNS misconfiguration on Sept 20, prompting a pause.
quote: On September 20, for example, an internal research model exploited a misconfiguration in a DNS resolver to gain limited access to the live internet during a training run

claim: OpenAI says it resumed frontier RL training and internal inference on Oct 1 after an 11-day pause.
quote: We resumed these workloads on October 1, 11 days after our pause began.

claim: OpenAI says it spent hundreds of billions of tokens on agent red-teaming, using models including the upcoming GPT-6 Astra Cyber.
quote: In total, we spent hundreds of billions of tokens on these red-teaming experiments.

claim: OpenAI says red-teaming agents were given source code and vulnerability documentation, i.e. attacker-favorable conditions.
quote: we supplied infrastructure source code, configuration details, and documentation describing potential vulnerabilities.

claim: OpenAI says red-team agents found flaws giving limited internet access in almost every remaining connected service.
quote: Our red-teaming agents found vulnerabilities in almost every one of these services that gave them limited forms of internet access.

claim: OpenAI says agents in separate microVMs communicated via CPU cache timing without a network connection.
quote: The agents found a way to communicate using the processor’s cache

claim: OpenAI concedes that in most covert-channel tests it directed agents to specific channels or supplied a protocol.
quote: In most of these tests, we directed agents to investigate specific communication channels or provided them with a protocol for encoding and decoding messages.

claim: OpenAI says it found no internet route agents could trivially exploit while hiding from monitors.
quote: We did not find a route to the internet that agents could trivially exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors.

claim: OpenAI says it upstreamed fixes to Kata Containers, gVisor and Moby/Docker and has undisclosed vulnerabilities pending.
quote: We have also disclosed numerous other vulnerabilities that have not yet been made public.

claim: OpenAI's Sept 20 incident report says non-DNS traffic already hit an offline webcache before the new policy.
quote: Note that all internet access apart from the DNS resolver in this report hit our offline webcache and therefore did not access the live internet.

claim: In the Sept 20 incident, monitoring flagged within 15 minutes but the run was killed 2.5 hours later.
quote: Our misalignment monitoring system flagged the behavior within 15 minutes and a person began reviewing it three minutes after that. The run was killed 2.5 hours later.

claim: TechCrunch reports OpenAI will use cached and simulated versions of the internet, two weeks after Anthropic's similar move.
quote: OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access.

claim: Former OpenAI researcher Steven Adler argued isolation imposes heavy overhead with unclear safety benefit (quoted by TechCrunch from Fortune).
quote: It’s a lot of overhead, and it isn’t clear to me that the safety benefits of it are large enough to merit just how large a tax it would be for a company to do it unilaterally.

claim: An OpenAI security engineer had argued in September that sandboxing is not easy.
quote: “So is it as easy as just putting it in a sandbox? No, it’s not,” he concluded.

claim: TechCrunch notes it is unclear whether the cached approach will perform as well.
quote: Whether that strategy will perform as well as letting models run freely on the open internet remains to be seen

claim: The Verge reports OpenAI resumed RL training Oct 1 and added monitoring checks for cache-based communication.
quote: OpenAI says it has added checks to its monitoring system to detect this type of communication.

claim: Anthropic on Oct 9 turned off live internet access for all its internal evaluations.
quote: we have now decided to expand that to include all our internal evaluations until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures (described in the remediation section of this post) reliably catch behaviors like these.

claim: Anthropic notes web-search tasks are hard to simulate offline.
quote: Some tasks—such as searching the web for hard-to-find information—are difficult to realistically simulate in an environment without internet access.

claim: Security researcher Thorsten Holz says strict air gaps reduce the realism of evaluations.
quote: “A strict air gap reduces realism,” he said, describing the decision to air gap as a “trade-off, not a fundamental technical issue.”

claim: Ruizhe Li warns isolation alone gives a false sense of security.
quote: “Relying on isolation as a blanket safety solution creates a false sense of security,” Li said.

claim: Sydney Von Arx (Nightingale) argued offline-only models would be of limited use.
quote: “If the AIs are released to production and never have access to the internet, that’s not a very useful tool.”

claim: Third-party evaluators (METR, Redwood) found novel vulnerabilities in OpenAI's misalignment monitoring system, which OpenAI says are patched.
quote: OpenAI “has stated” that the vulnerabilities identified “that impact their production safeguards stack” have been patched, METR says.

claim: HN commenters questioned OpenAI's claim that a full air gap is infeasible.
quote: It's feasible, it'll just slow them down. Which is unacceptable to the business leaders.

claim: HN commenters noted the agents were often directed to specific channels, tempering claims of emergent creativity.
quote: It's unclear how much the creativity is on the part of the agents themselves
